questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Shakespeare wrote many plays.

options.text: Many plays were written by Shakespeare.
Many plays was written by Shakespeare.
Many plays have be written by Shakespeare.
Many plays has been written by Shakespeare.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Shakespeare wrote many plays."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "many plays" at the beginning of the sentence.
 
• Change the active verb form "wrote" (simple past) to "were written" (simple past passive).
 
• Since "plays" is plural, the plural auxiliary verb "were" must be used instead of "was."
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Shakespeare."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Many plays were written by Shakespeare."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"Many plays was written by Shakespeare." – Incorrect subject-verb agreement; "plays" requires "were."
 
• **Option 3: **"Many plays have be written by Shakespeare." – Grammatically incorrect verb construction.
 
• **Option 4: **"Many plays has been written by Shakespeare." – Incorrect tense (present perfect) and subject-verb agreement.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Do greenhouse gases cause global warming?

options.text: Is global warming caused by greenhouse gases?
Are global warming caused by greenhouse gases?
Does global warming caused by greenhouse gases?
Do global warming caused by greenhouse gases?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure for interrogative sentences (Simple Present): **Is/Am/Are + Subject + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent?**
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Do greenhouse gases cause global warming?" (Simple Present).
 
• To convert to passive voice: The object "global warming" becomes the new subject.
 
• Since "global warming" is singular, the auxiliary verb "Is" is used at the beginning.
 
• The main verb "cause" changes to its past participle form, "caused."
 
• The original subject "greenhouse gases" becomes the agent following the preposition "by."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Is global warming caused by greenhouse gases?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"Are global warming caused by greenhouse gases?" – Incorrect subject-verb agreement; "global warming" is singular and requires "Is."
 
• **Option 3: **"Does global warming caused by greenhouse gases?" – "Does" is used in active voice; passive voice requires a form of the verb "to be."
 
• **Option 4: **"Do global warming caused by greenhouse gases?" – Incorrect auxiliary verb and incorrect subject-verb agreement.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

Will the project have been completed by the research team before the deadline?

options.text: Has the research team completed the project before the deadline?
Is the research team completing the project before the deadline?
Will the research team complete the project before the deadline?
Will the research team have completed the project before the deadline?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Future Perfect Tense** in an interrogative form.
 
• Passive voice structure for Future Perfect (Interrogative): **Will + Object + have been + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject?**
 
• To convert it into the **Active Voice**, the structure should be: **Will + Subject + have + Past Participle (V3) + Object?**
 
• The subject in the passive sentence "the research team" becomes the subject of the active sentence.
 
• The object "the project" becomes the object of the active sentence.
 
• The verb phrase "have been completed" changes to "have completed" in the active voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Will the research team have completed the project before the deadline?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Has the research team completed..." – Incorrect because it uses the **Present Perfect** tense.
 
• **Option 2: **"Is the research team completing..." – Incorrect because it uses the **Present Continuous** tense.
 
• **Option 3: **"Will the research team complete..." – Incorrect because it uses the **Future Simple** tense instead of the Future Perfect.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

Why aren't benign tumours rejected by the body?

options.text: Why don't the body reject benign tumours?
Why won't the body reject benign tumours?
Why doesn't the body reject benign tumours?
Why can't the body reject benign tumours?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Simple Present Tense** in an interrogative (negative) form.
 
• Passive voice structure for Simple Present (Interrogative Negative): **Wh-word + am/is/are + not + Object + Past Participle (V3) + by + Agent?**
 
• To convert it into the **Active Voice**, the structure should be: **Wh-word + do/does + not + Subject + Base Verb (V1) + Object?**
 
• The agent in the passive sentence "the body" becomes the subject of the active sentence.
 
• Since "the body" is a **singular** third-person subject, the auxiliary verb **"does"** (specifically "doesn't") must be used.
 
• The verb "rejected" (V3) changes back to its base form "reject" (V1).

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Why doesn't the body reject benign tumours?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"Why don't the body..." – Incorrect because "the body" is singular and requires "doesn't" rather than "don't."
 
• **Option 2: **"Why won't the body..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense from Simple Present to **Simple Future**.
 
• **Option 4: **"Why can't the body..." – Incorrect because it changes the meaning of the sentence to **ability/possibility** (Modal verb).

questions.question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.

Between the advantages of being an Indian citizen, freedom to worship one's own god is of utmost importance for the orthodox.

options.text: freedom to worship one's own god is
of utmost importance for the orthodox.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the preposition "**Between**" in part A of the sentence.
 
• The preposition "**Between**" is generally used when referring to two distinct people, places, or things.
 
• The preposition "**Among**" is used when referring to more than two things or when talking about a collective group (like "the advantages").
 
• Since the sentence discusses one advantage out of a larger set of advantages of being a citizen, "**Among**" is the grammatically correct choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"**Among** the advantages of being an Indian citizen, freedom to worship one's own god is of utmost importance for the orthodox."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "being an Indian citizen,"** – This part is grammatically correct as it functions as the object of the prepositional phrase.

questions.question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

This song is not befitting _______ the Independence Day Celebration.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**for**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The preposition **"for"** is used to indicate the purpose or suitability of something.
 
• In this sentence, the phrase "befitting for" is correct as it conveys the idea of appropriateness for the Independence Day Celebration.
 
• **Other options:**
 
 
• **"to"**: Incorrect, as it does not fit the context of appropriateness or purpose.
 
• **"on"**: Incorrect, as it refers to a specific time or date rather than suitability.
 
• **"by"**: Incorrect, as it refers to agency or means, not suitability.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"This song is not befitting **for**__ the Independence Day Celebration."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
__
 
• **Usage of "for":** This preposition is commonly used to indicate the purpose, suitability, or intended recipient of something.
 
• **Example:** "This dress is perfect for__ the party."
 
• **Common Prepositional Errors:**
 
 
• **"To":** Often confused with "for," but it indicates direction, not purpose.
 
• **"On":** Refers to specific dates, surfaces, or positions, not suitability.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.<
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
 
• This question involves rearranging the jumbled sentences to form a coherent paragraph. 
 
• **Sentence B is the first sentence** following S1: 
 
 
• "She was left alone, quite alone, as she had always wished to be left." 
 
• This sentence logically follows S1 as it continues the idea of Sofia being left alone after her mother and sister departed. 
 
 
 
• **Sentence A follows** because it delves into Sofia’s childhood experiences and habits: 
 
 
• "As a child, when some wrong or injustice had been done her, she had cried all alone, when she was in bed, in the dark, and the habit had remained with her." 
 
• This sentence explains her emotional state and further develops her character. 
 
 
 
• **Sentence D is the third sentence** because it describes her current emotional state in detail: 
 
 
• "Now, alone in the great drawing room, beneath the brightly lighted chandelier, her hands inert, her head resting against the back of her chair, her face wore an expression of great sorrow, the vivid reflection of a serious inward conflict." 
 
• This sentence connects her past emotions with her present solitude and sorrow. 
 
 
 
• **Sentence C is the fourth** as it brings in the realization of her grief and solitude: 
 
 
• "Certainly in these moments of complete solitude the consciousness of a great grief came over her." 
 
• This sentence ties the narrative together and leads smoothly into S2. 
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **BADC**. 

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"Sofia stood listening to the noise of the departing carriage which bore away her mother and sister. She was left alone, quite alone, as she had always wished to be left. As a child, when some wrong or injustice had been done her, she had cried all alone, when she was in bed, in the dark, and the habit had remained with her. Now, alone in the great drawing room, beneath the brightly lighted chandelier, her hands inert, her head resting against the back of her chair, her face wore an expression of great sorrow, the vivid reflection of a serious inward conflict. Certainly in these moments of complete solitude the consciousness of a great grief came over her; the sentiment of the reality, long repulsed, became clear, distinct, and cruel."

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

If I __would be laid off again__, I would seriously consider a career switch.

options.text: were to be laid off again

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**3**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The given sentence is an example of the **second conditional**, which is used to describe hypothetical or unlikely situations.
 
• In a second conditional sentence, the correct structure is **If + past simple, would + base verb**.
 
• The underlined phrase "**If I would be laid off again**" is incorrect because "**would**" is not used in the "**if**" clause.
 
• Option 3, "**were to be laid off again**," correctly uses the "**were to + base verb**" structure, which is appropriate for hypothetical situations.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"If I were to be laid off again, I would seriously consider a career switch."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "will be laid off again" is incorrect because the first conditional uses "**if + present simple, will + base verb**." However, this sentence describes a hypothetical situation, not a real possibility.
 
• **Option 2:** "had been laid off again" is incorrect because it suggests a past unreal situation, which would require a third conditional structure: "**if + past perfect, would have + past participle**."
 
• **Option 4:** "No improvement required" is incorrect because the underlined part does not follow the correct grammatical structure for the second conditional.
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence.

"Startups ______ a cultural shift from job seekers to job creators by fostering entrepreneurial opportunities nationwide."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2: drive***

 
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"Startups"**, which is a **plural noun**.
 
• According to the rules of **subject-verb agreement**, a plural subject requires a plural verb (the base form of the verb without an 's').
 
• Since the sentence describes a general fact or ongoing state in the present tense, **"drive"** is the correct form to match the plural subject.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: drives***
 
 
• This is **incorrect** because "drives" is the third-person singular form. It would be correct if the subject were singular (e.g., "The **startup drives** change").
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: driving***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. A present participle (ending in -ing) cannot function as the main verb of a sentence on its own; it requires an auxiliary verb like "are" (e.g., "Startups **are driving** a shift").
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: driven***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. "Driven" is a past participle and needs a helping verb to form a complete thought (e.g., "Startups **have driven** a shift" or "A shift **is driven** by startups").
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement Rule**: In the present tense, most verbs only change their ending for the third-person singular (he/she/it). For plural subjects (they), the verb remains in its base form.
 
• **Vocabulary Note**: In this context, to **"drive"** a shift means to be the primary cause or force behind a significant change in behavior or mindset within a society.
 
• **Unicorns**: As mentioned in the passage, a "unicorn" in the business world refers to a privately held startup company valued at over $1 billion.

questions.question: The word “flourishing” in the passage most nearly means ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 4: thriving and growing***

 
 
• In the context of the passage, **"flourishing"** is used to describe sectors like fintech, edtech, and e-commerce that are experiencing **"remarkable growth"** and **"gaining global recognition."**
 
• The word derives from the Latin *florere* (to bloom), and in a business or economic context, it refers to an entity that is prospering, expanding, and reaching a state of high success.
 
• The surrounding text mentions that these sectors are **"addressing local challenges"** and contributing to the production of **"unicorns,"** which reinforces the idea of vigorous health and expansion.
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: declining***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. "Declining" is an antonym (opposite) of flourishing. The passage describes a surge in growth, not a decrease.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: ignoring***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. "Ignoring" refers to a lack of attention and does not fit the description of an active, growing economic sector.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: struggling***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. While startups may face challenges, the passage uses "flourishing" to highlight the **success** and **powerhouse** status of the ecosystem, which is the opposite of struggling.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Synonyms**: Prospering, burgeoning, blooming, successful, robust.
 
• **Antonyms**: Withering, fading, failing, stagnant, declining.
 
• **Usage in Business**: When an "ecosystem" or "sector" is flourishing, it means the environment is conducive to success, leading to high investment, innovation, and job creation.
 
• **Context Clue**: The use of the word **"surge"** earlier in the passage acts as a context clue, suggesting upward momentum and rapid development.

questions.question: Which of the following best summarizes the main idea of the passage?

options.text: India’s startup growth is mostly centered in a few large cities with little government support.
The startup ecosystem in India is shrinking due to lack of innovation.
India’s startup ecosystem is expanding rapidly due to government initiatives, technology adoption, and widespread collaboration, contributing significantly to economic and employment growth.
Startups in India only focus on local markets without global ambitions.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 3: India’s startup ecosystem is expanding rapidly due to government initiatives, technology adoption, and widespread collaboration, contributing significantly to economic and employment growth.***

 
 
• The passage emphasizes **"remarkable growth"** and India's status as the **"third-largest startup hub globally."**
 
• It specifically credits the **"Startup India" initiative** for providing financial and regulatory support, matching the "government initiatives" part of the summary.
 
• It mentions **"tech-savvy professionals"** and **"internet penetration"** (technology adoption) and the **"synergy among incubators, accelerators, investors, and the government"** (widespread collaboration).
 
• Finally, it notes the **"economic growth and employment generation"** caused by over a hundred unicorns and the shift to becoming "job creators."
 
 
 
• ***Option 1: ...mostly centered in a few large cities with little government support.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text states the government's role is **"pivotal"** and that tier-2 and tier-3 cities are **"increasingly contributing."**
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: The startup ecosystem in India is shrinking...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The entire passage focuses on **growth, flourishing sectors, and expansion.**
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: ...only focus on local markets without global ambitions.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The passage mentions startups are **"gaining global recognition"** and fueled by the ambition to become a **"global startup powerhouse."**
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unicorns**: As defined in the passage, these are startups valued at over **$1 billion**. India having over a hundred of them signals a very mature and high-value ecosystem.
 
• **Cultural Shift**: The passage highlights a transition from a **"job seeker"** mentality to a **"job creator"** mentality, which is vital for long-term economic sustainability.
 
• **Sector Success**: The "flourishing" status of **fintech, edtech, and healthtech** shows that Indian innovation is heavily focused on using technology to solve practical problems in finance, education, and healthcare.
